# Supabase user insert conflict handling (2026-01-31 17:39Z)

_**User**_

In `@supabase/migrations/20260131000000_initial_schema.sql` around lines 88 - 127,
The INSERT in function public.handle_new_auth_user can raise duplicate-key
errors; modify the INSERT into public.users (performed in handle_new_auth_user)
to include an ON CONFLICT clause targeting the unique key(s) (at minimum
auth_user_id, and optionally google_email) and handle conflicts by either DO
NOTHING or DO UPDATE to upsert the profile fields; for example, use ON CONFLICT
(auth_user_id) DO UPDATE SET google_email = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.google_email,
public.users.google_email), google_full_name =
COALESCE(EXCLUDED.google_full_name, public.users.google_full_name),
google_profile_picture = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.google_profile_picture,
public.users.google_profile_picture) so the trigger is idempotent and avoids
duplicate-key failures.

Updated the `handle_new_auth_user` function to add an `ON CONFLICT` clause on `auth_user_id`. The INSERT now handles conflicts by updating existing rows with `COALESCE` to preserve existing values when new values are NULL.

This makes the trigger idempotent and prevents duplicate-key errors when:
- The trigger runs multiple times for the same user
- A user record already exists with the same `auth_user_id`

The `ON CONFLICT (auth_user_id) DO UPDATE SET` clause updates only the Google profile fields (`google_email`, `google_full_name`, `google_profile_picture`) using `COALESCE` to keep existing values when the new values are NULL.

Note: This handles conflicts on `auth_user_id`. If you also need to handle conflicts on `google_email` (a different user with the same email), we can add a separate conflict handler or a composite unique constraint. Should I add that as well?
